coverage: Weekend edition, week of Nov 2 to 6, preview of Nov 9 to 13
moodReason: The S&P 500 just posted its worst week since April 2025 and its fourth straight weekly loss, led by an AI and chip rout after the midterms. A hot jobs report has markets pricing a December Fed hike, and Tuesday's CPI report could add to that pressure.

stories.headline: Midterm results trigger the worst S&P 500 week since April 2025
stories.what: The S&P 500 fell 2.7% for the week to 7,376.86, its fourth straight weekly loss, after a 4.36% plunge on Thursday. The Nasdaq entered a correction and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index lost about 12% for the week.
stories.why: Democratic wins raised fears of tighter oversight and local halts on data center construction, threatening the AI spending boom that has driven most of this year's gains. The Magnificent Seven lost about $1 trillion in value on Thursday alone.

stories.headline: Hot October jobs report pushes December Fed hike odds near 80%
stories.what: Employers added 165,000 jobs in October, far above forecasts, and unemployment eased to 4.1%. Traders raised the odds of a quarter-point hike in December to about 78%, and LSEG data puts it near 80%.
stories.why: A tighter Fed raises borrowing costs and pressures stock valuations, especially richly priced tech. The dollar firmed after the report.

stories.headline: October CPI on Tuesday is the week's big test
stories.what: The October consumer price report is due Tuesday at 8:30 a.m. ET, with inflation expected to rise to 3.9% year over year from 3.7%. Producer prices follow on Friday, and about 10 Fed officials speak during the week.
stories.why: A hot reading would all but lock in a December hike and could extend the selloff, while a soft one could fuel a relief rally.

stories.headline: Oil posts its biggest weekly drop since 2022 on Iran peace hopes
stories.what: Brent fell more than 16% for the week to $98.32 and WTI lost nearly 13% to $90.83 after Iran reportedly sent a nuclear proposal to Washington through Qatar. Energy stocks fell about 11% to 12% for the week.
stories.why: Cheaper oil eases inflation pressure but hit energy stocks hard. Risk remains: tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz continued, and one analyst puts the chance of renewed fighting at 80%.

stories.headline: Chip stocks bounce Friday as Treasury yields ease for the week
stories.what: The semiconductor index rose 4.2% on Friday, with AMD up 11% and Nvidia up 2.8%, lifting the Nasdaq 1.1%. The 10-year Treasury yield ended the week at 4.86%, down 8 basis points, though breadth stayed weak.
stories.why: The rebound suggests some dip buying, and strategists at LPL and Truist called the selloff a knee-jerk reaction. VIX near 25.6 shows nerves remain high.

stories.headline: Data center opponents gain power after the elections
stories.what: Democrats who campaigned partly on data center moratoriums won governor races in Texas and Georgia, and voters in dozens of local areas rejected or restricted projects. Goldman Sachs estimated temporary halts could affect about 45% of planned US data center expansion.
stories.why: Delays to data center builds would slow orders for chips, power and equipment. HSBC expects tighter oversight rather than broad moratoriums, and Goldman sees the effect as short-lived.

stories.headline: AI earnings ahead: CoreWeave, Applied Materials, Cisco, then Nvidia
stories.what: CoreWeave reports after Tuesday's close, with analysts expecting a loss of about $1.45 per share. Applied Materials and Cisco report later in the week, and Nvidia reports on November 17.
stories.why: These reports will show whether AI demand is holding up after the post-election rout. FactSet expects S&P 500 third-quarter earnings growth of about 31%.

watch.item: Earnings: Occidental, Constellation Energy, KKR, Take-Two
October CPI at 8:30 a.m. ET, expected 3.9% year over year. CoreWeave earnings after the close
Jobless claims, existing home sales, NY Fed's Williams speaks. Earnings: Applied Materials, Cisco

bottomLine: Last week broke the AI trade's momentum: the election raised real doubts about data center growth, and a strong jobs report revived the threat of a December rate hike. Falling oil and slightly lower yields are small cushions. Tuesday's CPI report is the key event, since a hot number would deepen rate fears while a cool one could spark a relief rally. Expect elevated volatility until CPI and Nvidia's results on November 17 give clearer signals.
